examples.note: Letters extract mostly correctly here, confirming corruption is concentrated in/around specific glyphs (control chars) rather than uniform scrambling, but digits are hit.

Confirms digit corruption is not isolated to the year in the document title: '7' in '2017' also renders as a control character (\x1a) here. This means ANY digit in this document's text layer is potentially wrong, not just the cover-page year string — table numbers extracted via text layer cannot be trusted either. Note the substitution is a consistent Caesar-like offset (each visual digit's ASCII code minus 29 gives the control-char byte observed: '4'=0x34-29=0x17, '5'=0x35-29=0x18, '7'=0x37-29=0x1a), so it is a systematic CMap remapping, not random corruption — but still unusable without re-deriving the mapping, which get_text() does not do.

p01_25.conclusion: Corruption affects digits as well as letters, via a consistent -29 byte offset in the broken ToUnicode CMap (verified: 0x17->'4', 0x18->'5', 0x1a->'7'). Confirmed via page 10: '2017' (a data-bearing year, not just the document title) extracts as '201\x1a'. This means routing logic AND any text-based numeric extraction (enrollment counts, percentages, cohort years) on this document are compromised if they rely on page.get_text(). Only image-based reading is reliable, unless the extraction engine is changed to apply the discovered -29 byte-offset correction to every character (untested beyond the 3 sampled digits, and letters appeared mostly correct in some regions — e.g. page 4 body text extracted cleanly — suggesting the corruption may be scoped to a specific font/character range rather than the whole document; do not assume the offset fix is safe to apply blindly across all text).

p26_50.summary: Digits ARE corrupted in the extracted text layer, not just letters — confirmed both in running headers and in body/prose text. This means the text layer is unsafe for ANY content decision on this document, including numeric routing heuristics, not merely for headings.

Digits 2,0,2,4,2,0,2,5 all render as control characters \x15/\x13/\x17/\x18, i.e. digits are corrupted identically to letters in the same string.

Only the final digit of '2024' was corrupted in this extraction (the '4'), showing the corruption is character-level and can affect a subset of digits within a single number, which is especially dangerous for silent-but-wrong extraction (a partially-corrupted number still looks numeric).

p26_50.conclusion: Both routing logic (deciding which extraction path to use per page) and any text-based value extraction (e.g., regex-pulling a percentage or dollar figure straight from get_text()) are compromised on this document. Digits inside ordinary sentences and inside table-adjacent prose are corrupted exactly like surrounding letters. Image-based (vision) extraction at 150 DPI is mandatory for pages 26-50, with no text-layer fallback for any field, including ones that look like they should be 'just a number'.

batch4_verdicts.sat_act_percentile_table: The 25th/50th/75th percentile table (Assessment: SAT Composite, SAT EBRW, SAT Math, ACT Composite, ACT Math, ACT English, ACT Writing, ACT Science, ACT Reading) is entirely on page 19, directly under the C9 heading. Every data cell in all three percentile columns for every assessment row is printed BLANK - no numbers, no 'n/a' text, no dashes. This is consistent with Caltech's test-blind policy for this cycle; it is a fully empty table, not a text-extraction failure.
batch4_verdicts.c10_c11_c12_headings: C10 heading appears at the bottom of page 20 (its data table starts on page 21). C11 heading appears mid-page 21 (GPA-range table, all data cells blank). C12 heading appears lower on page 21 (Average HS GPA box, blank). So: C10 on pages 20-21, C11 on page 21, C12 on page 21.
batch4_verdicts.column_position_encoded_grids: Two clear cases in this range: (1) page 22, C15/C16-style same-line 'Yes □ No □' pairs where only box position marks the answer (e.g. C15 'No' checked, C16 'By (date)' option checked among three mutually exclusive line-items). (2) page 24, D5 'Indicate all items required of transfer students' - a 6-row x 5-column grid (Required of All / Recommended of All / Recommended of Some / Required of Some / Not Required) where each row's single checkmark's COLUMN position is the entire signal (e.g. Interview and Standardized test scores are marked 'Not Required' while the other four items are marked 'Required of All'); reading this by presence-of-mark-only without tracking column position would be meaningless.

section_j_notes.location: Pages 41-42 (Section J, item J1, the CIP disciplinary-areas-of-degrees-conferred table).
section_j_notes.military_science_row: Prints as a SINGLE COMBINED ROW labeled 'Military science and military technologies' with CIP code column value 'CIP 28 and 29' together — NOT two separate rows for 28 and 29. Confirmed by direct visual read of page 41.
section_j_notes.percentage_leading_zero_format: Percentages below 1.00 print WITH a leading zero (observed example: 'Business/marketing' Bachelor's = '0.90', not '.90'). No example in this document had a value below 0.10, so leading-zero behavior for very small percentages (e.g. 0.05) is inferred, not directly confirmed, from the 0.90 pattern plus the standard 'X.XX' two-decimal formatting used consistently across every populated cell in the table (40.90, 31.10, 5.10, 7.70, 14.50, 0.90).
section_j_notes.totals_row: Bachelor's column total = 100.20 (Diploma/Certificates and Associate columns both 0.00, as expected for Caltech which awards no diplomas/certificates/associate degrees). The >100 total is rounding drift across individually-rounded category percentages, not a data error to 'correct' downstream.
section_j_notes.only_bachelors_populated: Only the Bachelor's column has any nonzero entries anywhere in the J1 table for this institution; Diploma/Certificates and Associate columns are entirely blank/zero across both pages, consistent with Caltech being undergraduate-bachelor's-only plus graduate (graduate degrees are out of CDS J1 scope).
